positive_controls.argument: Maintained rationale, constraints and limitations let later work apply the appropriate control to the actual configuration.
Recoverable item and environment identities delimit the state to which each lifecycle control and independent conclusion applies.
Actual-state reconciliation reveals configuration or environmental differences that defeat the relied-upon control evidence.
Affected-claim analysis and proportionate authority routing determine which control evidence must be refreshed and which may be reused.
Owned versioned semantics make those risk-relevant expectations testable on both sides of the boundary.
Planned evaluability specifies the method, environment and independence needed to assess the particular control claim.
Evidence at the actual failure level tests whether the proposed lifecycle control survives the relevant interaction.
Accurate links reveal affected controls and evidence when a requirement, implementation or environment changes.
A challengeable argument exposes unsupported control claims, assumptions and counterevidence that the lifecycle work must address.
Anomaly identity, affected configurations and authorized residual disposition prevent known control failures from being silently dropped.
Scoped authority, semantic consistency and reality reconciliation qualify which model-based control claims are defensible.
Fresh identified results and explicit limits make control evidence available during continued change and operational response.
